info.title: Cobalt
info.author: Ewan Croft
info.description: A Bluesky client for the Wii U
info.details:
A native Bluesky / AT Protocol client for the Nintendo Wii U, built for Aroma.

Read your home timeline, threads, profiles, notifications and custom feeds; post, reply, quote and attach images; like and repost; search; mute and block. TV and GamePad are both first-class, including Off-TV Play.

Sign in with an app password, or through a hosted Wolfram OAuth node so your password never touches the console.

On first run, Cobalt asks you to scribble on the GamePad to make a private random seed (nothing can go online without one).

Cobalt can check this GitHub project for updates from its Updates screen. It only downloads when you press A.

changelog:
v0.15.0
Added

- Lists can now be created and edited from the Lists screen. X starts a new list, Y edits the selected one, and the inline editor changes the name, description and purpose (Curation or Moderation); a name is required and the rest may be cleared. List writes use Wolfram's wf_agent_graph_create_list, wf_agent_graph_update_list and wf_agent_get_record_typed, replacing the full record so createdAt and unknown fields survive. On a list's member screen, Y adds an account by handle or DID and X twice removes the selected member, with a clear working/failure line and a refetch only after success. Browsing and paging are unchanged. Host tests cover purpose mapping and editor validation, and snapshots cover the editor, list, member and add-member screens on both displays. (272: https://github.com/ewanc26/cobalt/issues/272)

- Starter packs can be opened from a recognized pack link in a post's More menu. The pack screen shows its name, creator, description and counts, lists the suggested accounts and included feeds in one bounded list, pages the members from the pack's underlying list, and opens a profile or feed from its row; B returns to the screen the pack was opened from, and a failed member page leaves the pack header and a retryable message. Read/use only: creating or sharing a pack remains deferred. Host tests cover link normalization and row bounds, and snapshots cover both displays. (271: https://github.com/ewanc26/cobalt/issues/271)

- Posts and accounts can be reported from More. A report chooses its target (the post's AT-URI and CID, or the account's DID), one of the standard reason types, and then asks again on a Send report/Cancel confirmation; B or Cancel sends nothing, and the success notice appears only after Wolfram confirms com.atproto.moderation.createReport. The action is hidden on your own post and your own account, and a request already in flight refuses a second one. Host tests cover the target/reason mapping and malformed or unknown values, and snapshots cover the menu, reason picker and confirmation on both screens. (269: https://github.com/ewanc26/cobalt/issues/269)

- Compositions can be saved as drafts instead of being posted or queued. Save draft in the confirmation list keeps the text, reply gate and reply/quote context in a separate versioned drafts.dat; the new Drafts entry on the home menu lists up to eight, A resumes one, and X twice deletes it. Drafts survive restart, a resumed draft is replaced rather than duplicated when saved or posted, and an image or multi-post thread is refused with a message rather than partly saved. The file is written atomically and a truncated or incompatible one is set aside. Host tests cover the codec, the list and the compose conversions; snapshots cover the list and a resumed draft. (276: https://github.com/ewanc26/cobalt/issues/276)

- Posts can be bookmarked from their More menu, which names the current state (Bookmark or Remove bookmark). Bookmarks are private to the account and have their own paged screen, reached from the Home menu; opening one opens its thread, and the Home timeline is left as it was. The calls are Wolfram's wf_agent_create_bookmark, wf_agent_delete_bookmark and wf_agent_get_bookmarks_typed, with wf_agent_get_posts_typed for the views; the page keeps the service's bookmark order and skips a post that has since been deleted. A failed toggle leaves the last confirmed state in place. Host tests cover the state, page order and cursor; snapshots cover the list and its menu on both screens. (267: https://github.com/ewanc26/cobalt/issues/267)

- Your own profile can be edited from its More menu. The editor starts with the current display name and bio, checks both against the service's byte limits before anything is sent, and only replaces the profile on screen once Wolfram reports the update succeeded. A failed write keeps the editor and its text open so it can be retried. Text fields only: avatar and banner uploads are follow-up work. Host tests cover the limits, empty fields and the editor's state, and snapshot cases cover the editor on both screens. (270: https://github.com/ewanc26/cobalt/issues/270)

- A thread can be muted or unmuted from its More menu. The entry names the conversation's root rather than the reply the cursor is on and calls app.bsky.graph.muteThread/unmuteThread through Wolfram, reporting the result on the status line; a failure leaves the open thread and its selection untouched. The protocol has no read for muted threads, so the menu reflects the roots this run muted and sign-out clears that record rather than claiming to know the account's full list. Snapshots cover the menu entry and host tests cover the root choice and the refused arguments. (274: https://github.com/ewanc26/cobalt/issues/274)

- Groups are in. R on Messages starts one: a name, then a comma-separated list of handles or DIDs, which Wolfram resolves, de-duplicates and checks. R on a group conversation opens its settings, where A renames it, Y adds members, X removes the selected one and R creates or enables/disables its join link, shown as https://bsky.app/chat/. The inbox recognises a group from the conversation's kind rather than its member count, and the group's details are read through Wolfram's typed getConvo/getConvoMembers. (107: https://github.com/ewanc26/cobalt/issues/107)
- A Credits screen, reached from the home menu, lists the repositories behind the stack: Cobalt, Indigo, Wolfram, Platinum and Channel Blue. Each https://github.com/ewanc26/... address is printed in full and the screen is passive, because the console cannot open a browser; B or the Back pill leaves it. The home menu gained a fourteenth entry.
- A link whose external view carries associatedRefs is hydrated through the public AppView into the card its record describes: an article with its publication and reading time, a gallery with up to four pictures, or a livestream marked live or ended. The request runs once, only when the card is first drawn, and is cached for the session; a link without a usable record, or a failed request, keeps the plain card. (102: https://github.com/ewanc26/cobalt/issues/102)

 Changed

- The host frame benchmark has a layout-only mode (tests/bench_main ... --layout): it still walks every layout, text-measurement and wrapping path but issues no SDL draw calls, so a scenario reports app-side microseconds instead of milliseconds that include the host's software blitter. In the measured run the steady timeline spends about 24 µs on layout against 1.5 ms for a drawn frame, and scrolling rises to about 120 µs as rows re-measure; normal mode and its output are unchanged. Host instrumentation only, with no Wii U timing implied. (289: https://github.com/ewanc26/cobalt/pull/289)

- Text measurements are cached until the post scale changes, so an idle screen no longer calls TTF_SizeUTF8 for the same labels, names and counters every frame. In the host frame benchmark the steady timeline falls from 121 measurements and 109 µs per frame to none; scrolling re-measures only the rows it reveals. Host-tested; the Wii U was not re-checked. (289: https://github.com/ewanc26/cobalt/pull/289)

- Wolfram is pinned to v0.44.2. The host and console CI jobs check out the same tag, so development, emulator and release builds use one Wolfram version. (289: https://github.com/ewanc26/cobalt/pull/289)

- Every screen outside Home now names itself in the title band instead of leading with the Cobalt wordmark and version. Settings, Account, Feeds, Credits, Diagnostics, Set up and Edit profile use the same page-title header as Notifications, Messages and Profiles, with a short note for context (what Settings controls, how many feeds are saved, the account handle); the version stays in Diagnostics' build line. On both screens the page's own name is now the largest line in the band. (289: https://github.com/ewanc26/cobalt/pull/289)

- Home uses one four-column grid on both screens instead of a four-column TV grid and a two-column GamePad list. Every entry keeps the same position on either screen, Down and Up move a full row everywhere (the TV previously moved two entries), and the GamePad's tiles grow from 40 px strips to 64 px finger targets with the focused entry's hint beneath the grid. (289: https://github.com/ewanc26/cobalt/pull/289)

- Profiles show their tabs as a visible Posts / Replies / Media strip under the page title, plus Likes on your own profile. The active tab is marked with an accent underline as well as colour, the left and right shoulders cycle the strip, GamePad taps pick a tab directly, and the tab name is no longer repeated in the title note. The More menu keeps its tab command. On TV the header is now one horizontal band — avatar, then name, handle, bio and counts, with Follow at the right edge — instead of a 266 px stack that pushed every post off the screen. Snapshots cover the Posts, Replies and Media states on both displays. (289: https://github.com/ewanc26/cobalt/pull/289)

- Notifications group the way the official client groups them: adjacent likes or reposts about the same post, within 48 hours of each other, draw as one row ("Ewan Croft and 2 others liked your post") using the newest actor's avatar and the row's subject. The "N new" badge still counts notifications rather than rows, and follows, replies and different posts keep their own rows. Unit tests cover the window, subject and reason boundaries and repeated grouping. (289: https://github.com/ewanc26/cobalt/pull/289)

- Release tag checks call Wolfram's reusable release-check workflow, pinned to v0.44.1. Cobalt still reads COBALT_VERSION itself, but the tag/version/changelog, on-main and CI gate checks are now shared rather than a second implementation. (wolfram232: https://github.com/ewanc26/wolfram/pull/232)

- Wolfram is pinned to v0.43.2. The follower and following lists are populated again, because the typed calls now read the arrays the endpoints send, and its public headers compile under -Wpedantic -Werror on Clang 16 and older. (wolfram226: https://github.com/ewanc26/wolfram/pull/226)

 Fixed

- A name no longer runs underneath what is drawn beside it. Notification rows fit the actor to the room the age leaves; message, member and join-request rows fit the name to the room their handle, "Group" or "You" leaves; and the profile, graph, credits, popup, quote and repost labels are fitted to their card. A page title now shares its band with the note, fitted to what each leaves, and drops the note rather than run past the edge. Host tests, snapshots and the Wii U build pass; Cemu was not re-checked for this. (289: https://github.com/ewanc26/cobalt/pull/289)

- Dynamic names and labels stay inside their rows. Post and quote authors, search and list rows, starter-pack members, menu items, saved-feed addresses and sign-in values now use one measured single-line fitter, which cuts at a UTF-8 boundary and counts its ellipsis in the width. A long display name no longer runs under a post's age or leaves its tile. Host tests, snapshots and the Wii U build pass; Cemu did not leave its boot pattern, so this was not re-checked there. (289: https://github.com/ewanc26/cobalt/pull/289)

v0.14.0
Added

- Gallery posts draw their first four pictures in the same row as an image post, and a link card names the publication and reading time when the external view supplies them (source.title/readingTime), falling back to the bare host otherwise. Both are read through Wolfram's embed-view parser, including the media half of a quote post; video posters and their duration are unchanged. (102: https://github.com/ewanc26/cobalt/issues/102)
- A Settings screen, reached from the home menu, with a Light/Dark theme switch, three post-text sizes (100%, 115% and 130%), a high-contrast palette and a Reset to defaults row. Theme and contrast apply immediately on both screens -- including the baked background gradient and header band, which are rebuilt when the palette changes -- and text scale reopens the post face and drops the renderer's text and wrap caches, so long posts re-wrap at the new size on the next frame. All three are saved in settings.dat, so they survive closing Cobalt; reset restores and saves the defaults in one action. The screen moved to src/app/settings_view.c rather than growing app_home.c. The audit behind it also fixed the surfaces that had been hard-coded white: control-prompt pills and popups now follow the theme, prompt key chips choose a readable ink over the accent, page titles use a header colour that stays white rather than the card surface (which turns dark), and the TV home grid shrinks its fourth row to fit the thirteenth entry. Host tests enforce WCAG AA contrast for the palette roles in all three modes, and snapshot cases cover high contrast on the popup, image viewer and chat screen. (compare: https://github.com/ewanc26/cobalt/compare/v0.13.0...main)

v0.12.0
Added

- A video whose playlist is a master playlist shows the length of one variant (the lowest bandwidth), followed once, at most two playlist fetches per video. (102: https://github.com/ewanc26/cobalt/issues/102)
- Message requests can be accepted or declined. On Messages, Y lists the requests; A accepts the highlighted one, which joins the inbox and opens, and X declines it, which removes it from the list. Each is one press and one request, nothing is sent on entry, and a failure is shown and not retried. Groups are still open. (107)
- A video's poster shows its length, read from the video's HLS playlist with Wolfram's wf_embed_video_playlist_duration. The playlist is fetched off the frame loop, only when the poster is drawn, and once per playlist. A master or live playlist, or a failed fetch, shows no duration. Needs Wolfram's unreleased wf_embed_video_playlist_duration (on Wolfram main, PR 217); it is not in the pinned v0.41.0. (102)

 Changed

- On the TV, the selected post in the timeline and thread shows as much of its text as fits in the right-hand column. A longer post ends in a "More below" line, and L and R scroll its text one line at a time. The list selection does not move while scrolling, and moving to another post starts its text at the top. The GamePad layout is unchanged. (111)

 Fixed

- Going back to a thread fetches its conversation again. The return stack remembers which thread each screen showed, so after a nested unwind the outer thread no longer shows the inner conversation. (110)
- Backing out of a thread opened from a profile that was itself opened from a thread no longer bounces between the profile and the outer thread. Each screen returns to the one it came from, down to the timeline, through a return stack in place of the single return slots. The snapshot suite now walks that chain. (110)
